questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the line types that can appear on a Receivables transaction?
options: Merge line
Item (revenue) line
Tax line
Freight line
questions.explain: There is no 'merge line' on a transaction; merging is a separate customer-maintenance process, not a transaction line type.

questions.q: What location does tax determination primarily consider?
options: The bill-to location only, regardless of where goods ship
The ship-to location, along with the item's nature and the customer's exemption status
The business unit's headquarters address
The transaction source
questions.explain: Tax is generally determined based on the ship-to location, the item or service, and whether the customer holds a relevant exemption.

questions.q: What are the two ways freight can be configured on a transaction?
options: Only as a tax line
Freight is never tracked separately from revenue
One flat freight line per transaction, or freight calculated per item line
Freight must always equal the tax amount
questions.explain: Freight can be a single line covering the whole shipment, or allocated across individual item lines, depending on configuration.

questions.q: In the Northwind Fixtures Co. / Harborline Retail Group example, why was tax only calculated on $10,000 of the $12,000 in item lines?
options: Because freight is always tax-exempt
Because tax is never applied to the first line on an invoice
Because Harborline's credit limit was exceeded
Because the $2,000 installation labor line was non-taxable in Harborline's state
questions.explain: The installation labor line was non-taxable, so the 7% tax rate only applied to the $10,000 taxable fixtures line.

questions.q: Does AutoAccounting use the same sourcing rule for freight as it does for revenue?
options: No — freight has its own separate AutoAccounting sourcing rule, distinct from the revenue account rule
Yes, freight always posts to the same account as revenue
Freight is never accounted for separately
Freight is only relevant for credit memos
questions.explain: AutoAccounting maintains a distinct sourcing rule for the freight account so freight amounts can be tracked separately from product revenue.
